correctness.rationale: Direct Frobenius normal/tangent basis gives the rank-one projector and 2x2 step overlap. The frame derivative yields exact continuous rotation R(sqrt(2)*pi); the step discriminant (cos(delta)-1)(9cos(delta)+7)/4 is negative for N>=3, giving rho=cos(pi/N), and its traceless remainder squares to -omega^2 I. This algebra proves the closed finite-N power and singular values. Strict contraction is a consequence of three spanning normals. Taylor expansion of rho^N, N theta, and the skew/symmetric decomposition proves the sharp N-times-error limit. A standard-library checker passed 206 finite checks; the infinite claim relies on these written identities rather than numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: Closed-loop transport is a natural benchmark: endpoint bases agree, so any amplitude loss and geometric-angle defect belong to the numerical transport itself. The exact spectral damping cos(pi/N)^N, nonnormal norm-loss correction, and positive leading operator-error coefficient make the benchmark useful for detecting errors in covariant projected integrators and for calibrating timestep effects in low-rank adjoint computations. The result is not merely the generic first-order method estimate or a reparametrization of continuous holonomy; it quantifies specific finite-step phenomena. The homogeneous, exact-projector scope is openly limited.
